items.title: Regeni family lawyer says govt must acknowledge ruling and sever ties with Egypt
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, 28 SET - Giulio Regeni's family lawyer said Monday that the Italian government must acknowledge a Rome court ruling finding three Egyptian security officials guilty of the student's abduction in Cairo in January 2016 and must therefore sever ties with Egypt. items.description: It was the latest wave in a displacement crisis that has been building in Somalia's Lower Shabelle region for a decade, and there is no sign it is reversing. items.description: Ayanle Hassan, Qoyste's son, told SJS that his father, who was diabetic, fell ill on Friday night and was rushed to hospital, where he was pronounced dead. The late Qoyste was a veteran journalist and one of the most remarkable radio journalists in Somalia, known for his distinctive and memorable voice. He first worked as an archive manager at the Ministry of Labour of the Somali central government in the 1980s before joining the print media in Mogadishu in the early 1990s, as the country descended into civil war. items.title: Regeni family lawyer says govt must acknowledge ruling and sever ties with Egypt
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, 28 SET - Giulio Regeni's family lawyer said Monday that the Italian government must acknowledge a Rome court ruling finding three Egyptian security officials guilty of the student's abduction in Cairo in January 2016 and must therefore sever ties with Egypt. "Now our government, too, must acknowledge this, demand compensation for damages as requested by the State Attorney's Office, and sever ties with a country that—far from being safe—tortures and kills even citizens of so-called friendly states," said Alessandra Ballerini, after the three got 10 years each in jail in absenbtia
